findings.title: Worker pre-main cleanup closes a descriptor reused by a linked library
findings.evidence: A real shared-library initializer closed and reused the inherited number for its own /dev/null; the crate's before_main then closed it. Final harness log SHA-256 84550457ed04d9698891b9fd586f4357047584a4f9690e1cfb1e2b8ef0dd4877.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained AUD-012 two-crate harness. Its linked-library constructor reuses the inherited descriptor, then the worker initializer runs and the child verifies the descriptor.
findings.expected: Only descriptors inherited from the parent are closed; a descriptor opened by a linked library remains open.
findings.observed: The linked library's reused descriptor was closed and the harness exited 1.
findings.impact: A native dependency loses its descriptor and may malfunction or use the wrong resource later; cleanup can make the worker appear clean. No direct secret disclosure was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Clean inherited descriptors at the spawn/exec boundary before library constructors, using the ordinary-stack launcher, or use a design that does not rely on numeric identity after constructors.
findings.requiredVerification: The retained harness must pass after the fix, followed by the full Linux/macOS worker suites and ordinary/malformed/protected-stack launch regressions.

confirmations.evidence: No additional defect confirmed; accepted and platform-pending limitations remain documented.
No tags or GitHub releases; Cargo publish=false; no canonical release binary procedure.

limitations: One Medium finding blocks affected native integrations.
Android and iOS were not run; macOS and Windows evidence is exact-SHA CI rather than local execution.
The independent coverage run measured 91.21% and recorded two profile-write refusals; 97.41% is not independently confirmed.
No exhaustive compiler-level erasure proof or canonical binary reproducibility claim is made.
This is not a security certification or release acceptance.
